Clara (AcmeEng): Hey team, during our midday POC run we're seeing a burst of 502/503s when concurrent requests hit ~120 rps. Clients report partial responses and timeouts.
Dan (AE): Thanks for flagging, Clara. Can you paste a sample request/response and the exact timestamps? Also what model & region are you on?
Clara (AcmeEng): Model: open-redwood-13b, region: eu-west-1. Seen between 12:07 and 12:12 UTC. Quick curl shows a 503: `curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." -d '{"model":"open-redwood-13b","input":"hi"}'` -> HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
Ben (Support): Copying triage. Likely capacity/backpressure. Can you grab a request-id from the client (x-rw-request-id) if present? Also, any retry/backoff in client?
Clara (AcmeEng): Request IDs: rw-req-20260321-7a2f, rw-req-20260321-7a30. Client has an exponential backoff but it retries immediately up to 3 times.
Ben (Support): OK. Looking at our side — checking logs for those req ids.
deply-bot: (automated) autoscaler: scale-up triggered for pool "eu-west-1-prod" at 2026-03-21T12:08:45Z, reason: cpu_spike, target_replicas=12
Erin (Oncall): I see the cluster hit CPU 92% on the serving nodes and our scale-up took ~40s to provision new pods (cold-start on specialized GPU instances). There's also queue backlog spike; burstpool exhausted.
Ben (Support): That's consistent. Autoscale delay + exhausted burstpool => request queueing leads to upstream 5xx from the runtime. Quick mitigation: enable emergency fallback to a lower-memory quantized variant and temporarily increase burstpool tokens.
Gina (Solutions): For the POC we can spin up a temporary Dedicated buffer (billed) to guarantee burst capacity. Dan — want me to quote short-term burst pricing?
Dan (AE): Yes please. Clara — would you accept switching to the quantized variant for the demo window? It reduces latency and uses less memory.
Clara (AcmeEng): OK to try quantized but need to confirm output quality is acceptable. Also curious on whether rate limits triggered; clients saw 429s briefly as well.
Ben (Support): 429s were from local client-side throttling + upstream backpressure. Not our rate limit policy. I'm going to enable a canary routing to `open-redwood-13b-q8` for 20% of your traffic now. Command: `POST /v1/routes/canary {"route":"acme-poc","model":"open-redwood-13b-q8","percent":20}`
Erin (Oncall): Done — canary routing active. Also increased burstpool from 50 -> 150 for the duration of the POC window. Expect immediate reduction in queue length.
Clara (AcmeEng): After canary switch we see fewer 503s at 12:10:20. Still some timeouts at high concurrency.
Ben (Support): I'm tailing logs: runtime reports `kv_cache_miss` spikes and some kernels falling back to CPU exec on startup. Adding a warm-up step helps. Can you run a short warmup workload: `for i in {1..50}; do curl ...; done` to populate KV cache?
Clara (AcmeEng): Running warmup now. Looks like failure rate drops to ~0.5% from ~8%. Nice.
Frank (Security): Quick note — customer submitted the security questionnaire earlier. I still need the exact ACLs and KMS key ARN used for the POC private logs export to finish the review. Clara, can you share the KMS key name or allow our team read access?
Clara (AcmeEng): Sharing via the form now. Also, any PII scrubbing on logs by default?
Ben (Support): By default we redact prompt content for hosted demo logs unless you opt-in to detailed logging. We can provide sanitized logs for audit.
Gina (Solutions): Pricing update: short-term burst add-on is $X/day (quoted privately), or we can provision a small Dedicated pool for the POC week at a flat rate. Dan will follow up with an official quote.
Dan (AE): I'll send the quote and contract addendum. Clara: would a 24-hour Dedicated trial work to avoid these autoscale cold starts?
Clara (AcmeEng): That would be fine if it's economical. For now the canary + warmup seems stable enough; we'll validate quality.
Erin (Oncall): Operational note: we'll add a 60s warmup policy for short-lived POCs going forward and recommend enabling burstpool for demos. Filed as internal ops doc change.
Ben (Support): Action items: 1) Ben/Erin keep burstpool up for next 2 hours; 2) Gina/Dan deliver pricing; 3) Frank complete security review once KMS info received; 4) Clara to run regression checks on outputs.
Clara (AcmeEng): Running regression suite now — initial samples look OK on quantized variant. Will report back by EOD. Thanks for quick help! :pray:
Dan (AE): Thanks everyone. Marking this thread as the POC throttle triage — I'll follow up on quote and contract.
Ben (Support): Closing loop — keep me pinged if error rate >1% after warmup.
Erin (Oncall): FYI, we observed a similar pattern with other demos; tracking an infra ticket for faster GPU spin-up (AUTOSCALE-789).
Clara (AcmeEng): All green here at 12:32 UTC — 0.2% 5xx after warmup. Good to close.
Dan (AE): Closing thread, will escalate next steps offline.
